raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including abdominal distension, abdominal pain, diarrhea, weight loss, and decreased stool caliber, along with the presence of a palpable mass in the left lower quadrant, are consistent with a diagnosis of sigmoid colon cancer. The CT abdomen and flexible sigmoidoscopy findings of a large heterogeneous proximal sigmoid mass with near-complete luminal obstruction further support this diagnosis. The surgical pathology showing a high-grade, poorly differentiated neoplasm with invasion through muscularis propria to serosal surface and lymph node metastasis also aligns with sigmoid colon cancer.

rejected.label: Colorectal adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: While this is a possible diagnosis, sigmoid colon cancer is more specific and directly corresponds to the location of the tumor described in the case.

rejected.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
rejected.why: The pathology findings do not support this diagnosis, as the tumor is described as a high-grade, poorly differentiated neoplasm, and immunohistochemistry results do not indicate a gastrointestinal stromal tumor.

rejected.label: Lymphoma of the colon
rejected.why: The pathology findings, including the description of the neoplasm and the immunohistochemistry results, do not support a diagnosis of lymphoma.

rejected.label: Poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma
rejected.why: The immunohistochemistry results, including negative staining for various markers such as keratin, CDX2, and others, do not support a diagnosis of poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma.
